data.turoyo: Bi walaye d Ḥəməṣ. W bi ziyaraṯe diḏe, d kətwa ġalabe basəmto šane, maksable foṯo gliṯo mi qadišuṯo du mḥasyo, bayn ak kine w az zadiqe, d kətwa. U ruḥmo du babayḏe. Roḥamwa u faṭəryarxo u babo du ʕAziz, d kətwa əšme Skandar.
data.translation: In the city of Homs. And on that visit of his, which was very pleasant indeed, he gained an open face from His Holiness, the late one, among the righteous and just, who was his father's friend. The patriarch used to love Aziz's father, whose name was Skandar.

summary: The supplied entry is an existing ksb discussion record, despite the reader’s claim that lookup found no entry. All inherited correspondence is retained in entry.md. The proposal adds the first structured stem/sense section, not a duplicate root.

Only kəsbina is textually attested here; 1pl plus d- comparison clause, with zero-marked i=ḥṭiṯayḏe. Arabic derivation is plausible and already discussed in the inherited notes, but no new etymological head text or finite Preterit/citation Infectum is asserted.

The sin construction is one collocation, not a sense split. Permitted lookup finds other guilt/sin idioms under mḥt, nfl and sym, but no matching kəsb combination. The edition’s on ourselves interpretation is retained without treating its wording as an overt Turoyo reflexive phrase.
Jan Beṯ-Şawoce: the supplied English is project machine translation. All semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo; English quotations are retained verbatim and are not edition translations.

The missing-root assertions are false for this supplied dataset: ksb is an existing correspondence entry, and round 1 proposes I.1 with kəsbina and a guilt collocation. None is repeated in the round 2 delta.

maksable recurs with foṯo gliṯo and coordinated dostaniye/ḥubo. It is provisionally placed in III by its surface ma- form, pending comparison with a loan paradigm or a contracted II; no etymological stem identity is asserted.
The social evaluator/source appears as qəm commanders, m- the patriarch, and me kul ḥa. b foṯo gliṯo at Jan 3.17/295 makes direct-object status uncertain there; the other tokens lack that b-.
The face expression is a single collocation in the existing idiom section. Searches of the permitted glossary lookup for foṯo gliṯo and maksab returned zero hits.

87/37: confirm kəsbina segmentation, citation forms and integration of the probable Arabic loan. Does the general acquisition verb combine productively with money and other objects, as suggested in the inherited correspondence? That broader range lacks a full corpus example here.

Clarify the relation of i=ḥṭiṯayḏe to the son: guilt incurred by what happens to him, rather than guilt committed by him? The possessive suffix and the wider family context need native-speaker review.
Confirm whether maksable belongs to III, a contracted II loan, or an m-prefixed acquisition paradigm distinct from I kəsbina; supply an attested Infectum before a full citation pair is published.
Does foṯo gliṯo denote favourable reception, standing, or bold access? Explain b foṯo gliṯo in Jan 3.17/295 versus bare foṯo in the other three attestations.
Jan adds independent acquisition evidence at the root level, supporting the broader acquisition meaning proposed in round 1; maksable does not by itself establish the finite paradigm of I kəsbina.
